entries.text:
Hi. What are we working on?

The Airtable plugin needs authorization before its tools will work. You can run `/mcp` in an interactive session to authorize it.

I can't do the authorization from here. This session is non-interactive, so the OAuth flow won't open, and saying so in chat doesn't grant it.

To authorize it, open an interactive Claude Code session and run `/mcp`. Pick the airtable server and follow the browser prompt. The Airtable tools will work after that.
make a png of s tick figure and open it in preview
I drew a stick figure and saved it to `/tmp/stick-figure.png`. It's open in Preview now.

He's cooler now. He has sunglasses, a red backwards cap and a smirk. One hand is on his hip and the other is throwing a peace sign. He's standing on a skateboard.

It's saved to `/tmp/stick-figure-cool.png` and open in Preview.
make t wavier and put it in a cirty with 1000 of them
The front of the crowd turned into a colorful mush, and the figures are too small to show their wobble. I'll push most of the crowd toward the back and make the front figures bigger and wavier.

There are 1000 of him now, skating down a street in front of a purple skyline at sunset. His limbs and head wobble now. Each one gets a random cap color, a random board, and either a peace sign or a big wave.

The front rows are still crowded and overlap a lot, so you can't make out individual figures there. I can spread them out or add a few big ones up front if you want.

It's open in Preview and saved at `/tmp/stick-city.png`. The script is `/tmp/stick-city.py`.

I built him as a 3D scene in `/tmp/stick-3d.html`, but I haven't seen it render yet. I asked Chrome to open it, and Chrome came to the front, but no window with it showed up in my screen capture. It may have landed in another space. A headless render timed out, so I have no screenshot.

In the scene, his arms, legs and body are wavy black tubes that keep wiggling. He has a white head, a red backwards cap, black sunglasses and a smirk. He rides a skateboard with yellow wheels. He stands on a street inside a ring of purple buildings, with an orange sunset sky. The camera circles him slowly, and you can drag to orbit or scroll to zoom. It loads three.js from a CDN, so it needs internet.

If Chrome shows a blank page, tell me and I'll debug it.
